question: How is the subtle level distinguished from the gross level in this triad?
premises: The same triad can be considered separately.
When considered separately it is called subtle.
Examples include intending to produce ṣaḍja, to play sweetly, and to speak words.
inference: The subtle level is the triad experienced as distinct intentional acts prior to their fused gross expression.
uncertainties: The mapping of the three examples to the three members of the triad is implied rather than stated explicitly.
plain_english: When that same triad is taken separately, it is called subtle, as in the distinct intentions: I make the ṣaḍja, I play sweetly, I speak words.
